tagline: The studio's front door on port 3010: one gateway that lazily starts each project's services and proxies LAN callers to them behind a shared gate secret.
summary: The on-device dispatcher (the "main gateway") runs on the studio Mac and lets laptops and other apps reach studio-hosted services through one address. A request to `http://<studio>:3010/<project-id>/...` is matched against a registry by longest path prefix, the gateway starts the target service if it isn't running, and proxies the call to its loopback port. Callers prove themselves with `x-dispatcher-gate-secret`.

Most projects sit behind their own **project dispatcher** (code-commit-summaries, code-control, my-gmail-manager, estimate-and-proposals, my-ops-tracker, finances-manager); the main gateway forwards to it and injects that project's secret, and the child only exposes paths listed in its storage's `dispatcher_exposed_endpoints`. The gateway keeps its registry, project catalog, access audit and per-project worker sessions in its own `on_device_gateway` Postgres, and the web admin shows projects, sessions and live worker terminals.
audience: You run a homelab "studio" Mac that owns the canonical databases for several Luckee projects.
You want laptops and other apps to reach those services without exposing each port on the LAN.
You operate the stack and need to see which workers are running and why.
notFor: Internet-facing traffic — upstreams must be loopback HTTP and the gateway is meant for the LAN.
A general-purpose reverse proxy or service mesh.
Projects that keep data locally and don't use the studio pattern.

capabilities.title: Prefix routing with lazy start
capabilities.detail: `dispatcher.services.json` / `registry_services` map `pathPrefix` → loopback `upstreamBaseUrl`; services with `spawn` config start on first request.

capabilities.title: Gate secret and admin secret
capabilities.detail: `x-dispatcher-gate-secret` on proxied routes; `x-dispatcher-admin-secret` on `/api/dispatcher/*` (except health); optional client IP allowlist and spawn roots.

capabilities.title: Project dispatchers
capabilities.detail: `gateway_projects` points at each child dispatcher; the child's endpoint catalog is loaded at runtime from its `GET /api/dispatcher/catalog`.

capabilities.title: Worker sessions
capabilities.detail: One table per project × tier (dispatcher, storage, api) records start, activity and end; `POST /api/gateway/jobs/reconcile-stale-sessions` stops idle workers.

capabilities.title: Admin web
capabilities.detail: `/dashboard`, `/dispatcher-detail-page` and `/gateway-admin-page`: projects, registry, sessions, sign-ups and users.

capabilities.title: Terminal dock
capabilities.detail: Live worker output over WebSocket (`node-pty` + `ws`) from `data/workers/{serviceId}.log`.

components.name: Main gateway
components.owns: Registry and proxy, lazy spawn, project dispatcher forwarding, secrets injection, `on_device_gateway` Postgres (`migrations/`), worker sessions, audit, admin and catalog APIs, terminal WebSockets.
components.doesNotOwn: Product data — each project's storage owns its own database and endpoint list.

components.name: Gateway web
components.stack: Next.js, Redux Toolkit, Supabase JS, xterm.js
components.owns: Admin UI, project/session tables, terminal dock. A server-side proxy validates Supabase sessions and calls the gateway with `GATEWAY_WEB_PROXY_SECRET`.

components.name: Console
components.owns: Listed in the registry for operator admin, but not cloned on this machine.

dataFlow: A caller (laptop API, another app) sends `GET/POST http://<studio>:3010/<project-id>/api/...` with `x-dispatcher-gate-secret`.
The gateway checks the secret (and IP allowlist), finds the longest matching prefix, and records the access.
If the target isn't healthy it spawns it (records a worker session) and waits for readiness.
It proxies to the loopback upstream — usually the project dispatcher, injecting that project's gate secret — which forwards only exposed endpoints to storage or the API.
Responses pass through unchanged; idle workers are stopped by the reconcile job.

trust.title: LAN callers
trust.detail: Must present `DISPATCHER_GATE_SECRET`. `DISPATCHER_GATE_INSECURE_ALLOW=true` in the example turns that off — don't leave it on.

trust.title: Gateway
trust.detail: Holds every project dispatcher's gate/admin secret and `DATABASE_URL` for `on_device_gateway`. Spawns processes only under `DISPATCHER_SPAWN_ROOTS`.

trust.title: Project dispatchers / storage
trust.detail: Accept only the secret the gateway injects and only their exposed endpoint list.

trust.title: Web admin
trust.detail: Supabase sign-in, then a server-to-server secret (`GATEWAY_WEB_PROXY_SECRET`).

commonTasks.title: Add a new project behind the gateway
commonTasks.when: A project gets a storage server and dispatcher.
steps: Follow `Add a new project dispatcher.md`: add a `gateway_projects` row (migration), worker session tables, and the child dispatcher's spawn config.
Seed the project's `dispatcher_exposed_endpoints` in its storage.
Add the injected secret env var and reload (`POST /api/dispatcher/config/reload`).

commonTasks.title: Expose one more endpoint
commonTasks.when: A caller needs a new path.
steps: Follow `Exposing a new endpoint.md`: add the row to the project's storage `dispatcher_exposed_endpoints`.
Reload the child dispatcher; no change to the main gateway.

commonTasks.title: Debug a stuck worker
steps: Open the project in the web admin and check active sessions and the terminal dock.
Stop/start the service (`POST /api/dispatcher/services/:id/stop|start`) or run the stale-session reconcile.

troubleshooting.fix: Wrong or missing `x-dispatcher-gate-secret`, or the caller's IP isn't in `DISPATCHER_ALLOWED_CLIENT_IPS`.
No registry prefix matches, or the child dispatcher doesn't list that endpoint as exposed.

troubleshooting.symptom: First call after idle is slow or times out
troubleshooting.fix: The gateway is spawning the worker. Raise the caller's timeout (e.g. `STORAGE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`) or keep the worker warm.
The service's `cwd` isn't under `DISPATCHER_SPAWN_ROOTS`, or `DISPATCHER_SHELL_INIT` / nvm isn't set up for that shell.
Create `on_device_gateway` and apply migrations, or set `GATEWAY_ALLOW_JSON_FALLBACK=true` for dev only.

glossary.definition: A per-project child (e.g. my-ops-tracker on 3095) that starts storage/API and enforces the exposed endpoint list.
A method + path in a project's storage `dispatcher_exposed_endpoints` the gateway may forward.
A recorded lifetime of a spawned dispatcher, storage or API process.

hubNotes: hub.local.json points at `~/github/luckee/on-device-dispatcher/...`, but the repos are at `~/github/on-device-dispatcher/`. Hub can't run this project until those paths are fixed.
Web port 3074 is also my-vercel-analytics' `webPortStart` in hub.local.json — running both at once will clash.
`on-device-dispatcher-console` is in the registry but isn't cloned. The same folder has an experimental `on-device-express-dispatcher-*` set (express gateway, storage, web) that isn't registered.
Projects that depend on this gateway: code-commit-summaries, code-control, my-gmail-manager, estimate-and-proposals, my-ops-tracker, finances-manager, make-it-sound-like-me, my-fundraise.
